scope.idea: A timeout-addressability repair is acceptable only if it restores client reconciliation without collapsing independent request accounting lineage.

evidence.claim: The direct caller-ID binding proof changed client-known timeout addressability from false to true while preserving the timeout and completion witness.
Two independent logical operations using the same caller-controlled ID collapse into one canonical request row with both attempt nonces and the second completion as winner.
The production-safe shape preserves a gateway-generated canonical internal_request_id and stores client correlation separately as a one-to-many relation.
The Gonka verification thread explicitly rejects the direct client-ID canonicalization proof patch as a production remediation.

past.summary: A client timeout could lose the only response-carried internal request identifier even though execution continued and completed.

present.summary: Binding the caller correlation directly to canonical request accounting restores local addressability, but upward storage verification exposes lineage collision when that caller value is reused.

future.summary: Client correlation remains a separate one-to-many lookup relation while internal request identity stays unique and gateway-controlled.

causalPath.statement: The client times out before receiving Gonka's generated internal request identifier while the request can still complete in the background.
The tempting proof patch promotes caller-controlled client correlation into the canonical request accounting identity.
At the timeout-addressability level the candidate repair passes: the client-known identifier can resolve completed accounting after timeout.
The parent accounting layer keys canonical request state by request_id plus escrow_id, while caller correlation is allowed to repeat across independent operations.
Two independent logical operations that reuse the same caller-controlled ID are represented by one canonical request row containing attempts from both operations.
The local repair therefore corrupts higher-level lineage: attempts 101 and 202 coexist in one row and the second completion becomes the winner, so the candidate is rejected as a production fix.
The safer design keeps canonical internal request identity unique and persists client correlation separately as a one-to-many relation.

navigation.reason: The candidate is green at the timeout-addressability level, so FCRP must move upward into the parent persistence/accounting contract before accepting the repair.

refactor.change: Use caller-controlled client correlation directly as the canonical request_accounting request identity.
refactor.expectedEffect: Restore post-timeout addressability using an identifier the client already knows.

recommendedReplacement.change: Keep gateway-generated internal_request_id canonical and persist client_correlation_id as a separate one-to-many mapping.
